summary: The comment argues that the FCC should strengthen hearings and CIPA enforcement to ensure a thorough review of the scientific evidence and legal precedents related to CIPA enforcement. The FCC is urged to conduct an independent, industry-neutral scientific assessment of RF exposure risks and implement transparent, evidence-based policies to protect public health. The comment calls for the FCC to consider ecological and health impacts of RF radiation before proceeding with rulemaking on cell towers and wireless infrastructure. It cites external evidence that new cell tower transmitters would increase involuntary exposure to RF radiation, which poses public health risks to humans and wildlife. The text argues against the sunset of E-Rate funding, citing concerns about the health and environmental impacts of 5G technology. The text argues against limiting or sunsetting E-Rate, emphasizing the need for continued funding to support broadband infrastructure and services. The comment cites experts from various institutions to argue against limiting or sunsetting the E-Rate program, emphasizing its statutory authority and regulatory requirements.
filer_raw: Theodora Scarato | Director of Wireless and EMF Program at Environmental Health Sciences
